text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- The Socialist Party, Albania's second biggest political force, said it will offer a pre-election contract to the Social Democrats and the Democratic Alliance Party.

- A Tirana court ordered a search throughout Albania for the last communist President Ramiz Alia, charged with crimes against humanity. Alia left jail after violence broke out in Albania in March and did not appear in court.
- A Tirana court ruled former interior minister Gramoz Ruci, a Socialist, will not be tried for crimes against humanity after prosecutors withdrew charges against him.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha said his Democratic Party would win planned parliamentary elections in June and opposed an extended mandate for an Italian-led European military force.

- A senior official of the disbanded communist secret police, the Sigurimi, wrote that they feared two well-known politicians were trying to topple communism. Both of them have been banned from running for parliament due to alleged links with the Sigurimi.
- Two Social Democratic Party leaders accuse forces close the Democratic Party and President Berisha of using violence against them. They added such forces threatened to destabilise Albania.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- President Berisha acknowledged failure in foreseeing the March "rebellion", insufficient work to consolidate the institutions and mistakes in selecting personnel.
- Lawyers for former communist interior minister Gramoz Ruci said they would bring a case against former secret police head Bashkim Gazidede for making a false denunciation against their client.
- A sunken ship with the bodies of 83 Albanians has been located at a depth of 800 metres off the southern Italy coast.
- Deputy Tomorr Malasi, an ex-speaker of parliament, has quit the Democratic Party parliamentary group, and listed himself as a member of the conservative party.
- Italian police have blocked 137 would-be immigrants and seized 675.6 kg of marihuana.
- Four people were killed on Sunday in a gang war that has gripped the southern town of Vlore. Two were killed in Fier in a clan vendetta.
- Bandits have killed and looted Albanians coming to and from Greece. Romanian troops of the eight-nation military force are not intervening to stop such acts, saying it is not within their mandate.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Democratic Party will win with a bigger margin than the Socialist Party, the paper said in a headline quoting President Berisha.
ALBANIA

- The Democratic Party wants to pass an election law under which 115 seats will be contended by direct representation and 40 by the proportional system. The number of seats allocated proportionally will be increased from 25 to 40.
